kind: CronJob

  name: image-scan-cron

    spec:
      template:

          initContainers:

  name: data-archiver
  namespace: nightly-backups

## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates CKAD proficiency in extending namespace-centric validation using core Kubernetes primitives: ConfigMaps, Secrets, CronJobs, InitContainers, PVCs, and NetworkPolicies. It also tests knowledge of jq for in-cluster JSON Schema validation and idempotent status updates.

## Key Concepts

- **Namespace-scoped configuration**: All resources operate within a single namespace boundary
- **CronJob with InitContainer tooling**: InitContainer prepares the environment (curl/jq) before the main validation container runs
- **JSON Schema validation using jq**: jq processes ConfigMap data against the fetched schema
- **PVC-backed logging**: Persistent storage preserves logs across job executions
- **NetworkPolicy egress control**: Restricts outbound traffic to only approved endpoints
- **Status persistence in ConfigMap**: Validation results are stored for auditing and downstream consumption

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: ns-config-schema-validator
  namespace: <target-namespace>
spec:
  schedule: "*/7 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: installer
            image: busybox
            command: ["sh", "-c", "wget -O /usr/local/bin/jq https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/download/jq-1.7/jq-linux64 && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/jq"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /usr/local/bin
          containers:
          - name: validator
            image: curlimages/curl:latest
            env:
            - name: API_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: validation-creds
                  key: api-key
            command: ["sh", "-c"]
            args:
            - |
              SCHEMA_URL=$(kubectl get configmap validation-config -o jsonpath='{.data.schema-url}')
              curl -s $SCHEMA_URL -o /logs/schema.json
              for cm in $(kubectl get configmaps -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
                kubectl get configmap $cm -o json | jq -s ".[0] * {data: .[1] | getpath($cm | split(\"-\")[1:] | map(.))}" /logs/schema.json > /logs/validation-$cm.json || true
              done
              curl -X POST http://validation-portal:8080/api/v1/validate -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" --data-binary @/logs/summary.json
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /usr/local/bin
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: validation-logs
          - name: tools
            emptyDir: {}
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Trade-offs

| Aspect | Trade-off |
|--------|-----------|
| **InitContainer vs. Custom Image** | InitContainer adds startup latency but keeps the main image lightweight and avoids maintenance of a custom image. |
| **jq Validation vs. Dedicated Validator** | jq is lightweight and universally available, but lacks full JSON Schema draft support. A dedicated validator (e.g., kubeconform) offers better accuracy at the cost of added complexity. |
| **PVC for Logs** | Provides durability and debugging capability but introduces storage overhead and potential bottlenecks in high-frequency runs. |
| **NetworkPolicy Egress** | Restricts access to only required endpoints, enhancing security but requires careful planning of all dependencies. |
| **ConfigMap Status vs. Custom Resource** | ConfigMap is simpler and requires no CRD management, but lacks built-in versioning and conflict resolution. |

    spec:

## Why This Question Matters for CKAD

This question validates mastery of **production-grade Kubernetes patterns** — not just textbook syntax. It combines seven CKAD concepts (CronJob, Job, InitContainer, ConfigMap, Secret, PVC, NetworkPolicy) in a realistic multi-tenant operational scenario.

## Key Concepts Tested

| Concept | Role in Pipeline |
|---------|-----------------|
| **CronJob** | Schedules periodic migrations with concurrency control |
| **Job** | Executes single migration attempt (created by CronJob) |
| **InitContainer** | Prepares SQL client before main container runs |
| **ConfigMap** | Versioned, injectable migration scripts without image rebuilds |
| **Secret** | Secure credential injection with namespace isolation |
| **PVC** | Persistent log storage for debugging and audit trail |
| **NetworkPolicy** | Enforces zero-trust network per namespace |

## Critical Design Decisions

1. **Why InitContainer for SQL client?**
   - Keeps main image minimal (security) and migration image separate from app image
   - Trade-off: adds startup latency and complexity

2. **Why PVC at /logs?**
   - Jobs are ephemeral; logs would be lost without persistence
   - Enables audit trail and post-mortem debugging

3. **Why NetworkPolicy egress restriction?**
   - Tenant database should only receive connections from migration Jobs
   - Prevents lateral movement in case of pod compromise

4. **Why probes on Job Pod?**
   - Liveness: ensures stuck jobs are restarted (but can cause issues with long migrations)
   - Readiness: typically irrelevant for Jobs, but included per question requirements

## Common Pitfalls Candidates Miss

- Forgetting `restartPolicy: OnFailure` (Jobs require explicit restart policy)
- Not handling ConfigMap subPath mounting (prevents live updates)
- Missing PVC lifecycle management (orphan storage, cost accumulation)
- NetworkPolicy blocking DNS (common exam/interview mistake)
- Not considering concurrent Job execution (data corruption risk)

## Real-World Extensions

- **Argo Workflows**: For complex multi-step migrations with retry logic
- **Flyway/ Liquibase**: Tool-based migrations with built-in versioning
- **External Secrets Operator**: Dynamic credential rotation without pod restarts
- **Cilium NetworkPolicy**: More expressive than standard K8s NetworkPolicy

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a periodic batch using CronJob with PV, ConfigMap-driven config, Secrets, and RBAC, plus resiliency and rollback.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob vs Job, ConfigMap, Secret, PersistentVolumeClaim, RBAC
- startingDeadlineSeconds, backoffLimit, preStop lifecycle
- readinessProbe and livenessProbe, serviceAccount scope

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: daily-processor
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  startingDeadlineSeconds: 3600
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 3
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: batch-job-sa
          volumes:
          - name: data-pvc
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: data-pvc
          containers:
          - name: daily-processor
            image: batch-processor:latest
            volumeMounts:
            - name: data-pvc
              mountPath: /data
            envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: cron-config
            env:
            - name: API_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: api-credentials
                  key: API_KEY
            readinessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /health
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 10
              periodSeconds: 30
            livenessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /ready
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 30
              periodSeconds: 30
            lifecycle:
              preStop:
                exec:
                  command: ["sh","-c","sleep 5"]
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you monitor backlog and guarantee idempotent processing across restarts?
- How would you rollback a broken patch to a previous CronJob manifest?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical use of ConfigMaps, envFrom, and volume mounting; checks how changes trigger controlled rollouts with an annotation-based restart cue; covers health checks basics.

## Key Concepts
- Deployments, ConfigMaps, envFrom
- Volumes and ConfigMap mounts
- Rolling restarts via PodTemplate annotations
- Readiness and Liveness probes
- Trade-offs: restart cost vs. up-to-date config, ConfigMap size impacts, security

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConfigMap skeleton
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: feature-flags
data:
  FLAG_A: "true"
  FLAG_B: "false"
---
# Deployment skeleton
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: feature-flag-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: feature-flag-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: feature-flag-service
      annotations:
        checksum.feature-flags: "{{ .Values.configMap.checksum }}"
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:alpine
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: feature-flags
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /config/flags
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
      volumes:
      - name: config-volume
        configMap:
          name: feature-flags
```

## Trade-offs Discussion
- **Restart Cost vs. Fresh Config**: Rolling restarts ensure configuration consistency but cause temporary availability reduction
- **ConfigMap Size Impact**: Large ConfigMaps increase annotation length and may affect API server performance
- **Security Considerations**: Environment variables expose config to process inspection; file mounts provide better isolation
- **Update Latency**: Annotation-based restarts are immediate but may be disruptive compared to hot-reload approaches

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests CKAD competencies including per-namespace controller patterns, ConfigMap/Secret integration, Deployment patching, RBAC configuration, and operational pause/resume with cooldown logic. It also validates understanding of observability through PVC-based logging and InitContainer provisioning.

## Key Concepts
- **Per-namespace controller design**: Controller runs within the target namespace rather than cluster-wide
- **RBAC**: ClusterRole with namespaced patch permissions for Deployments
- **ConfigMap/Secret integration**: Canary policy and credentials consumed as volumes or environment variables
- **Patch-based control flow**: Annotation-driven pause/resume mechanism
- **PVC-based logging**: Persistent storage for diagnostic data
- **NetworkPolicy**: Namespace-scoped egress restrictions to monitoring endpoints

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: canary-policy
data:
  threshold: "0.8"
  cooldown: "300"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: metrics-credentials
type: Opaque
stringData:
  api_key: ""
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: canary-controller
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: canary-controller
rules:
- apiGroups: ["apps"]
  resources: ["deployments"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "patch"]
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["configmaps", "secrets"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: canary-controller
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: canary-controller
  template:
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: canary-controller
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
      containers:
      - name: controller
        image: canary-controller:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        - name: policy
          mountPath: /config
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: canary-logs
      - name: policy
        configMap:
          name: canary-policy
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: canary-egress
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: canary-controller
  policyTypes: ["Egress"]
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: prometheus
```

## Trade-offs

| Aspect | Consideration |
|--------|---------------|
| **Per-namespace vs Cluster-wide** | Simpler RBAC and isolation, but requires separate Deployment per namespace |
| **Annotation-based pausing** | Non-invasive but relies on controller availability |
| **PVC for logs** | Provides persistence but requires storage provisioning |
| **InitContainer approach** | Increases pod startup time; consider sidecar pattern for production |
| **Polling vs Events** | Simple polling is easier to implement; watch API is more efficient but complex |
